an10.177:2.3: Here, as usual in the Suttas, “departed” (_peta_) just means someone who has died. They may end up in any realm. There is generally no specific “realm of the departed” or “realm of hungry ghosts” in early Buddhism. Instead, we find the old Vedic concept of the “realm of the forefathers” (_pettivisaya_). This concept is essential in Vedism, because the path to the realm of the forefathers for the father lay in having a son, and the son had to perform rites for his father. This idea is absent from Buddhism, and there is no relevance for a specific “domain of the forefathers”. It evolved into a more general “realm of the departed”, an evolution we can detect in a few verse passages in the early texts (see [thag3.14:1.2]() and note).
an10.177:6.4: Reading _na upakappati_ following BJT and PTS. The fact that the variants are not listed in MS suggests that the omission is an oversight.
